GuruFocus: Kinetik was $58.81, +7.5%, at 10:00 a.m. ET on Friday on potential acquisition interest from Targa Resources; Targa -1.4%; the move is 6 times Kinetik's typical day of 1.3%; other pipeline companies rose about 1%.

Investing.com: Vertex fell 7% on Friday morning. A Baird analyst said the delay is worse than moving sales back three months: it gives Otsuka and Vera time to entrench their approved rival drugs, Voyxact and Trutakna; Vertex's drug would launch closer to when both rivals get full approval with kidney-outcome data, while Vertex's comparable two-year data is likely more than a year away; and in a worst case the FDA is looking at a need to monitor an antibody level in patients. Otsuka and Vera both launched within the past year. Vertex was up 24% this year through Wednesday.

Citi kept its Buy rating and $585 target on Vertex and called the delay 'not thesis changing', while saying it adds regulatory uncertainty; 26 of 32 analysts rate the stock a buy; Vertex was -6.4% at the time.

themes.beneath: Reported: the moves and the report about the chips. My inference: Nvidia now carries two risks that are its own and not the industry's: a ratings agency's watch over how it is governed (the Wednesday note), and a report that barred chips reached China, which is a matter of export rules. Neither is about demand for its products, which is why Micron and Broadcom can rise without it. One more thing under the day: the 10-year yield is up 0.09 point, more than twice its usual day, and the stocks that follow rates most closely did not fall (Toll Brothers -0.1% where its usual rate implies -2.4%; r:10-year yield). So the bond move reads as money leaving safety on a strong day, in a thin market that closes at 2 p.m. ET, more than as a rates scare. That last part is inference.

themes.beneath: The argument is about what the FDA asked for, and nobody outside knows. The bear case, as the Baird analyst put it (opinion): the rivals get time to dig in; Vertex would launch about when they receive full approval with kidney-outcome data, while its own comparable two-year data is likely more than a year away; and at worst the agency is weighing a monitoring requirement for patients, which would make the drug harder to use (s7). The bull case (opinion): nothing about the drug's promise has changed (s8). In money, Vertex's fall is now about $7.9 bn (5.5% of $144.0 bn; n:VRTX), down from about $10.5 bn before the open. My inference: the price sits between the two views, closer to the bears, and the session moved it a quarter of the way back.

themes.mechanism: A correction to the earlier notes, which said the delay left Vera's drug alone on the market.
